title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost by shipping automated defaults and tooling that select batching, KV-prefix caching, and quantization profiles per-customer workload. This PR implements an initial autotune pass that: (1) applies conservative batching and cache defaults for common request shapes, (2) introduces a quantization profile registry and simple compatibility rules for hardware tiers, and (3) exposes a unit-economics dashboard + CLI tooling for teams to evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs.

Summary of changes: consolidated heuristic defaults into config/autotune/defaults.go; added quant profiles and compatibility matrix under model/quant_profiles/*.json; extended serving router to surface autotune hints and safe-fallbacks; added a small UI widget and a backend route for unit-econ telemetry (console/uecon); created a CLI command redwoodctl uecon snapshot to export per-route unit costs. Includes migration to add autotune_enabled flag on customer configs with a safe default (false for Dedicated/private by default).

Design notes: defaults are intentionally conservative — aim to reduce tail risk. Autotune runs offline and suggests changes; operators can opt-in to auto-apply for non-sensitive tenants. Quantization profiles are labeled by precision and hardware compatibility (e.g., int8-a100, int8-h100, fp16-t4). The unit-econ tooling aggregates token counts, GPU-seconds, and billing-weights to produce cost-per-1000-token and latency P50/P95.

Testing: unit tests for defaults heuristics and quant profile parsing (model/quant_profiles_test.go); integration test that simulates mixed-length traffic and verifies batching and cache hints are generated; e2e test that exercises redwoodctl uecon snapshot and the console route. Manual perf runs on staging showed a median token-cost reduction of ~11% for chat-heavy workloads and ~6% for single-turn generation when autotune suggestions are applied.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind tenant.autotune_enabled and feature flag ff:autotune-cost. Canary rollout to 5% of hosted tenants for 48h, monitor cost/latency and false-positive regressions (quality diffs). If any regression >1.5% in generation quality or >5% increase in request latency, auto-apply will be rolled back and flagged for manual review.

Backward compatibility: all changes are opt-in. Quant profiles are additive and do not change existing model artifacts. Migration adds a tenant flag with a migration job that defaults to "off".

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-4321 (autotune defaults), ENG-4410 (unit economics v1), SUP-1203 (customer request to reduce inference spend).
